History:
• Chief complaint: Severe left-sided throbbing headache beginning around midday today (a few hours ago).  
• Onset/Progression: Preceded by zig-zag visual lines and blurred vision (“aura”) in both eyes; pain intensity described as “horrible.” Patient uncertain whether onset was sudden or gradual.  
• Aggravating factors: Headache worsens with head/neck movement or leaning forward; photophobia (wearing sunglasses).  
• Associated symptoms: Nausea with two episodes of vomiting; photophobia; no fever, rash, speech difficulty, limb weakness, balance problems, or head trauma.  
• Previous episodes: One similar headache a few weeks ago lasting “a couple of days,” improved with rest and over-the-counter painkillers. No prior formal migraine diagnosis.  
• Patient concerns: Fear of brain tumor following personal research and friend’s family experience.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic illnesses: None reported.  
• Surgical/Hospitalizations: None mentioned.  
• Allergies: Not stated (missing).  
• Family history: Mother with migraines and under-active thyroid; no known family brain tumors.  
• Current medications: Microgynon oral contraceptive, taken for 3 months (dose/route/frequency not documented). Occasional OTC painkillers (names/doses not specified).  
• Social: Lives alone; works in fashion industry under high stress; non-smoker; no alcohol; little exercise.

Physical Examination:
• General: Appears photophobic (wearing sunglasses), otherwise conversant and oriented; no distress noted beyond headache.  
• Neurological (by history-based screen): No speech deficit; no motor weakness, numbness, or coordination problems reported.  
• Skin: No rash reported.  
• Vital signs: Not documented.

Impression:
• Likely migraine with aura.

Management Plan:
• Symptomatic relief:  
  – Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) or Co-codamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  – NSAID such as Ibuprofen or Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Education & reassurance: Explained clinical features consistent with migraine; low likelihood of brain tumor or meningitis.  
• Headache diary: Start daily log to identify frequency, duration, and potential triggers.  
• Follow-up: Review in one week; earlier if headache persists >2–3 days, worsens, fails to respond to medication, or if new neurological symptoms (limb weakness, visual changes, worsening neck pain) develop.  
• Future consideration: Discuss prophylactic migraine therapy at follow-up if attacks become more frequent or disabling.

Patient Summary:
Young woman with no significant past medical history presents with second episode of unilateral throbbing headache preceded by visual aura and accompanied by photophobia, nausea, and vomiting—most consistent with migraine with aura. No red-flag neurological features elicited. Provided analgesic plan, reassurance, and safety-net advice; scheduled short-term follow-up.

Key Takeaways:
1. Begin recommended analgesics (paracetamol/Co-codamol ± NSAID) at onset of headache.  
2. Maintain a detailed headache diary to track patterns and triggers.  
3. Seek immediate care if headaches worsen, persist beyond 2–3 days, or any weakness, vision loss, or severe neck pain occurs.

Next Steps:
• Implement headache diary immediately.  
• Trial of suggested analgesics; monitor response.  
• Primary care follow-up appointment in one week to reassess and consider prophylactic therapy if indicated.
